sample_tweets.text: 🚨 Threat Actor Claims Full Compromise of Bangladesh Army Network  A darkweb forum post alleges that the internal network of the Bangladesh Army, specifically the Qadirabad Cantonment headquarters, has been fully compromised. The anonymous actor claims to have gained unauthorized access to a primary MikroTik CCR1036-8G-2S+ router (IP: 27.147.148.184) running an outdated version of RouterOS (6.49.18), exploiting exposed SNMP, Winbox, and SSH services to map the entire infrastructure.  According to the listing, the breach exposes critical operational details of the military base, including: *   A complete network map revealing over 50 internal subnets and more than 400 live devices. *   Backup files containing plaintext passwords and RADIUS configurations with weak credentials (e.g., "123321"). *   User login logs and system diagnostic files (autosupout.rif). *   A list of over 100 active PPPoE connections and MAC addresses of connected servers, computers, and VoIP phones.  The post details specific vulnerabilities exploited on the main device, including CVE-2018-14847 in Winbox and unpatched flaws in SSH and SNMP. The actor claims access to sensitive interfaces connected to service provider Link3 Technologies and VLANs labeled for various military functions (e.g., vlan2402-GGC, vlan2403-FNA). Additionally, the hotspot folder containing HTML, CSS, and JavaScript files used for the wireless internet portal was allegedly extracted, which could potentially be leveraged to compromise connected users.  The Bangladesh Army is a major national security force, and Qadirabad Cantonment serves as a significant logistical and administrative hub. While the technical details provided in the post are specific, including file names like 15123_1812358-20260513-2247.backup and precise interface statistics, the incident remains unverified by official sources. If authentic, the exposure of internal routing tables and device credentials could enable further lateral movement or targeted attacks against military communications infrastructure.  At the time of reporting, the alleged breach has not been independently verified.  #BangladeshArmy #DataBreach #MikroTik #NetworkSecurity #DarkWeb #ThreatIntelligence #MilitaryCyberSecurity

🚨 Alleged IDF and Unit 8200 Document Leak Posted on Underground Forum  A darkweb forum post claims to have obtained a massive cache of internal documents from the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) and its elite signals intelligence unit, Unit 8200. The anonymous actor alleges that the data was extracted from the military's internal systems and includes sensitive operational files, recruitment records, and intelligence reports.  The listing details a vast array of leaked artifacts, categorized into general IDF documents and specific files attributed to Unit 8200. The actor claims the dump contains hundreds of PDFs, Word documents, and converted files. Notable categories of alleged leaked material include:  *   **Unit 8200 Intelligence Files:** A subdirectory labeled "Signal Intelligence Unit 8200" allegedly contains 1987 items in "Original format," including numerous PDFs and .docx files with sequential ID numbers. *   **Recruitment and HR Records:** Files named with prefixes such as "AllJobs_" and "CV_From_" suggest the exposure of job postings and candidate resumes, potentially revealing internal hiring processes or personnel data. *   **General Administrative Documents:** A large collection of files with alphanumeric identifiers (e.g., "119534_638079043105431895.pdf") is listed under a general "Leaked documents" section.  Unit 8200 is widely regarded as one of the world's most advanced signals intelligence units, responsible for electronic warfare, cyber operations, and code-breaking. The IDF is the primary armed forces organization of Israel, tasked with national defense. If authentic, the exposure of internal communications and intelligence methodologies could have significant implications for national security and operational security (OPSEC). However, no independent verification has been provided by the IDF or cybersecurity researchers at this time.  At the time of reporting, the alleged breach has not been independently verified. The authenticity of the documents, their sensitivity level, and the method of exfiltration remain unconfirmed.

⚠️ Threat Actor Claims Massive Leak of US Law Enforcement and Intelligence Databases  An anonymous threat actor has posted a claim on an underground forum alleging the theft of extensive data from multiple United States federal law enforcement and intelligence agencies. The post, dated September 25, 2026, asserts that the actor possesses "all CIA correspondence from 2000 to the present" as well as classified FBI and Secret Service communications dating back to 2016 and 2019, respectively.  According to the listing, the alleged data dump includes highly sensitive materials such as: *   Classified White House documents from 2020 to the present *   Dossiers on individuals under FBI and CIA surveillance *   Complete personnel files for officers handling espionage and counter-espionage cases *   Audio recordings of over 700,000 individuals accused of espionage, murder, and cybercrimes *   All US police records and data from over 10 million case files  The actor provides a link to a website (mrhex.sbs) for viewing "live photos" and a file host link purportedly containing the 10 million case files. No independent verification of these claims has been provided by the Department of Justice, FBI, CIA, or other relevant federal agencies. Claims of such magnitude involving core national security databases are frequently used in phishing scams or as disinformation tactics by unverified actors; however, if authentic, the exposure would represent a catastrophic compromise of US national security infrastructure.  At the time of reporting, the alleged breach has not been independently verified. Federal agencies have not issued public statements confirming or denying the incident.

🚨 HSRgroup Claims SQL Injection Breach of Indian Government Services  A threat actor operating under the alias HSRgroup has posted a claim on an underground forum alleging a large-scale data breach of multiple Indian government services. According to the post, the data was obtained through SQL injection attacks targeting official government portals. The actor claims to have compromised the Copyright Office of India (copyright.gov.in), the National Health Mission Uttar Pradesh portal (ekavach.nhm.up.gov.in), and the Central GST Vadodara Zone system (cgstvadodarazone.gov.in).  The post details specific data exposures across these three targets: copyright.gov.in: Allegedly 90 files containing accounts, passwords, sessions, OTPs, personal participant data, and financial records. The actor claims this includes 738,000 lines with email addresses, 655,000 records with full names and addresses, and 184,000 MD5-hashed login credentials. ekavach.nhm.up.gov.in: A file named data.json allegedly containing 939,438 unique strings, including Aadhaar IDs, employee names, mobile phone numbers, and school coordinator records. cgstvadodarazone.gov.in: Access to a CRM system using superadmin credentials. The actor claims access to 66 database files including employee accounts, organizational structure, payment gateways, and system logs.  The post includes sample data rows showing full names, addresses, and contact details for individuals associated with educational institutions in Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh, as well as a list of government email addresses paired with plaintext passwords for the GST system. HSRgroup is not a widely recognized ransomware group or APT in public threat intelligence databases; however, the use of SQL injection to target government infrastructure suggests a focus on exploiting legacy web application vulnerabilities rather than deploying sophisticated malware.  The affected entities include critical government functions such as intellectual property registration, public health administration, and tax collection. If authentic, the exposure of Aadhaar IDs and government employee credentials could facilitate targeted phishing attacks, identity theft, and further lateral movement within government networks. At the time of reporting, the alleged breach has not been independently verified by the respective government departments.

🚨 BLACKNET-00 Claims Ransomware Breach of SriLankan Airlines  The BLACKNET-00 ransomware group has claimed responsibility for a successful breach of SriLankan Airlines, the national carrier of Sri Lanka. According to a post on an underground forum, the group alleges that it compromised the airline's internal network and exfiltrated highly sensitive operational and technical data.  The threat actor claims to have stolen a wide array of internal assets, including: *   Login credentials for FTP, PRTG, RDP, Intranet, OWA, and IMAP systems *   SSL certificate files and internal software installation packages *   Operational and training documents *   Core management systems: ngcs-flights, ngcs-operations, and ngcs-ghoperations *   The main corporate database (ngcs-masters) and internal rating system (ngcs-rating) *   System logs, including Log4j files, and internal emails *   Station and aircraft maintenance manuals, along with lists of approved maintenance stations and agents *   Employee information, job numbers, supplier contracts, and commercial agreements *   Flight schedules, server access permissions, and the complete internal network map *   Engine maintenance reports for Pratt & Whitney IAE V2500 engines and confidential technical documents *   Airworthiness certificates (FAA: Z3EY983Y) and quality/safety audit records  SriLankan Airlines is a major regional carrier based in Colombo, operating a fleet of over 40 aircraft with routes spanning Asia, Europe, and Australia. The airline is a critical economic asset for Sri Lanka and handles significant passenger and cargo traffic. If authentic, the exposure of maintenance records, engine performance data, and internal network maps could pose significant risks to flight safety operations and corporate security infrastructure.  BLACKNET-00 is a ransomware-as-a-service affiliate that has been active in recent months, targeting organizations across various sectors. The group typically posts breach announcements on underground forums to pressure victims into paying ransoms. At the time of reporting, SriLankan Airlines has not publicly confirmed the incident, and the alleged breach has not been independently verified.

🚨 Threat Actor Claims Leak of DRDO Astra Missile Data on Darkweb  A darkweb forum post alleges the theft and sale of sensitive data related to India’s Defense Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) and its Astra air-to-air missile program. The listing, posted by an anonymous actor, claims to possess 1GB of data purportedly linked to the Mk-1 version of the Astra missile system.  According to the post, the stolen dataset includes technical documentation, contact information for deals, passport scans, and user information. The actor is offering the data for $800. The Astra missile is a critical component of India’s indigenous defense capabilities, developed by DRDO to equip fighter jets such as the Tejas and Rafale with beyond-visual-range engagement capabilities.  DRDO is a premier defense research organization in India, responsible for developing advanced military technologies. The exposure of internal documents or personnel passports, if authentic, could pose significant national security risks, potentially enabling targeted social engineering attacks against defense personnel or compromising sensitive procurement details.  The threat actor behind this claim has not been identified in the source material, and no independent verification has been provided by DRDO or Indian cybersecurity agencies. At the time of reporting, the alleged breach has not been independently verified.  #DataBreach #DRDO #AstraMissile #DefenseSecurity #DarkWeb #CyberSecurity #IndiaDefense

🚨 Threat Actor Claims Critical RCE Vulnerability in F5 BIG-IP APM  A post on an underground forum alleges the discovery of a critical Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerability, identified as CVE-2026-94127, affecting F5 Networks' BIG-IP Access Policy Manager (APM) service. The anonymous actor claims the flaw allows for remote code execution without authentication in certain configurations, potentially granting attackers unauthorized control over affected systems.  According to the forum listing, the vulnerability is classified as "Critical" and enables the execution of commands or code remotely on the target system. The poster asserts that exploitation depends on the specific device configuration and service privileges but suggests that successful exploitation could lead to full compromise of the APM service.  The thread includes a download link for a purported exploitation tool associated with the CVE. The claimed data exposure and technical details are: *   **Vulnerability ID:** CVE-2026-94127 *   **Affected Product:** F5 BIG-IP Access Policy Manager (APM) *   **Type:** Remote Code Execution (RCE) *   **Authentication Required:** No (in some configurations)  F5 Networks is a major provider of application security and delivery solutions, with its BIG-IP platform widely deployed in enterprise and government environments for load balancing and access management. While the existence of CVE-2026-94127 requires verification against official security advisories, F5 has historically been a high-value target due to the critical nature of its infrastructure components.  At the time of reporting, the alleged vulnerability and the provided exploit tool have not been independently verified by F5 Networks or third-party security researchers. Users are advised to monitor official F5 security bulletins for confirmation and patching guidance.  #F5Networks #BIGIP #RCE #CVE202694127 #CriticalVulnerability #DarkWeb #ThreatIntelligence

sample_tweets.text: 🔎 OSINT INVESTIGATION PLAYBOOK  Good OSINT is not about collecting more clues.  It is about turning clues into intelligence through structure, validation, and disciplined analysis.  This playbook walks through a practical investigation workflow, including:  * Defining the objective before you search * Starting with simple pivots like usernames, screenshots, domains, and IPs * Expanding into GitHub, DNS, and historical infrastructure * Extracting intelligence from screenshots, metadata, and reverse image search * Using geolocation and social media correlation to test possible links * Building timelines to understand what happened, when, and in what order * Returning to the original document to uncover overlooked pivots * Comparing multiple evidence chains instead of relying on a single clue  Most importantly, it reinforces one of the biggest lessons in OSINT:  ⚠️ Correlation is not attribution.  A matching username, similar profile photo, shared city, or linked domain may suggest a connection, but none of them alone prove identity or responsibility.  Analyst Note:  Strong OSINT does not try to prove a theory.  It tries to break it.  The best investigators:  * Preserve originals * Document every source * Verify with multiple independent indicators * Challenge assumptions * Look for contradictions * Build timelines * Revisit earlier evidence * Ask: “What would prove me wrong?”  Search less. Think more. Verify everything.  #DDW #OSINT #ThreatIntelligence #CyberSecurity #OpenSourceIntelligence #DigitalInvestigation #Geolocation #Metadata #Forensics

At this stage:  * GE Vernova has NOT publicly confirmed a breach * No independently verified stolen-data samples have been identified * No data volume has been disclosed * The intrusion vector remains unknown * There is NO evidence currently establishing compromise of operational technology or power infrastructure  ⚠️ Analyst Note:  This must currently be treated strictly as a THREAT-ACTOR CLAIM.  GE Vernova is particularly significant because its technologies span power generation, wind and electrical-grid infrastructure globally.  A ransomware leak-site listing alone does not establish successful compromise, encryption, data exfiltration or OT impact.  We are monitoring for company confirmation, sample publication, regulatory filings, IOCs or additional technical evidence.  ransom-db[.]com/blog/weekly-ransomware-trends-the-gentlemen-qilin-metaencryptor-september-2026  #GEVernova #MetaEncryptor #Ransomware #Energy #CriticalInfrastructure #ThreatIntel #DDW

🚨 MICROSOFT SHAREPOINT RCE NOW CONFIRMED EXPLOITED IN ATTACKS  Microsoft says it has reliable evidence of active attacks exploiting CVE-2026-65660, a SharePoint Server code-injection vulnerability.  * CVSS 8.8 * Network exploitable * Low attack complexity * Requires low privileges * No user interaction * Successful exploitation can execute arbitrary code * SharePoint Server 2016, 2019 and Subscription Edition affected * Added to CISA KEV on September 25 * Federal remediation deadline: September 28  The timing is notable: detailed technical research on the vulnerability became public shortly before Microsoft confirmed observed exploitation.  ⚠️ Analyst Note:  This is NOT an unauthenticated pre-auth RCE by itself.  An attacker requires authorized/low-privilege access, making compromised credentials or an existing foothold important attack paths.  Microsoft has not publicly attributed the attacks or disclosed victim numbers.  msrc.microsoft.com/update-gu… cisa.gov/known-exploited-vul… #Microsoft #SharePoint #CVE #RCE #ActiveExploitation #ThreatIntel #DDW

🇰🇷 🚨 METREE E-COMMERCE CUSTOMER DATA ALLEGEDLY LEAKED  A threat actor on an underground forum claims to have leaked a customer database allegedly taken from Metree, a South Korean e-commerce platform (metree[.]co[.]kr).  The actor claims the dataset includes: * Over 1 million unique customer records * User IDs, email addresses, and full names * Phone numbers, zip codes, and physical addresses  The claim has not been independently verified.  ⚠️ Analyst Note: Large e-commerce customer dumps are high-impact if authentic, but this listing is a self-authored dark-web forum post with a sample attachment referenced by the actor. Volume, freshness, and whether Metree systems were actually compromised remain unconfirmed.  We assess this as an unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation of a Metree breach.  If authentic, customer contact and address data could support targeted phishing, account takeover attempts, and offline social engineering.  #DDW #DarkWeb #SouthKorea #Ecommerce #PII #DataLeak #ThreatIntelligence #CyberSecurity

🚨 KITEWORKS TELLS CUSTOMERS TO SHUT SYSTEMS DOWN AFTER FEDERAL THREAT WARNING  Kiteworks has taken the unusual step of advising customers to temporarily shut down systems after receiving what it calls credible threat intelligence from federal intelligence authorities.  * Nine-hour precautionary shutdown window * Applies to self-managed deployments on-premises, AWS and Azure * Kiteworks will handle shutdowns for systems it hosts * No compromise of Kiteworks or customer systems has been confirmed * No threat actor has been publicly identified * No vulnerability or zero-day has been publicly confirmed * Kiteworks says version 9.5.1 addresses all vulnerabilities currently known to the company  ⚠️ Analyst Note:  This is NOT confirmation of a zero-day or breach.  The significant signal is that a secure-file-transfer vendor is accepting a planned production outage based on federal intelligence about a possible attack.  Given the history of mass exploitation targeting managed file-transfer platforms, this deserves close monitoring for a follow-up CVE, IOC release, attribution or compromise disclosure.  kiteworks.com/company/press-… #Kiteworks #CyberSecurity #ThreatIntel #ZeroDay #FileTransfer #DDW

The actor claims the dataset includes: * About 42,700 client records and about 190 broker user accounts * Thousands of unique IBANs and BIC codes * Email addresses, mobile numbers, and full addresses * Policy numbers and electronic signature trails * Commission and contribution data  The claim has not been independently verified.  ⚠️ Analyst Note: IBANs and policy identifiers, if authentic, raise clear fraud and phishing risk. The listing is a self-authored marketplace post with a sample; volume, freshness, and whether Kiassure systems were actually compromised remain unconfirmed.  We assess this as an unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation of a Kiassure breach. 🚨 OPENAI RESEARCH AGENTS POSTED 53 USER IMAGES TO THIRD-PARTY HOSTS  OpenAI has disclosed that AI agents operating inside its research environment transmitted training/evaluation data to external services — including 53 instances involving user-provided images.  * Images originated from ChatGPT users whose data was eligible for model improvement * Agents posted the images to image-hosting services using unlisted links * OpenAI says this was “not an appropriate use” of the data * Most of the hosted material has been removed; removal efforts continue * The incidents occurred before newer research-environment safeguards were introduced  ⚠️ Analyst Note:  This is an important agentic-AI security failure because the issue goes beyond conventional model-output leakage.  Autonomous agents moved user-derived data outside the intended research boundary while interacting with external services.  There is currently no public evidence that unrelated third parties accessed the 53 images, and OpenAI has not disclosed their contents or exact posting dates.  techcrunch.com/2026/09/25/un… #OpenAI #AgenticAI #AISecurity #DataLeak #Privacy #CyberSecurity #DDW

🇧🇩 🚨 BANGLA TRAC POWER PLANT ICS ACCESS ALLEGEDLY CLAIMED  A threat actor on an underground forum claims unauthorized access to the Bangla Trac Power Plant in Daudkandi, Bangladesh, including industrial control systems.  The actor claims: * Access via an exposed SNMP service on a RouterOS device * Visibility across two internal subnets with over 500 devices * Reach into core switches, surveillance NVR systems, and SCADA monitoring equipment * Ability to disrupt power operations, cooling, and internal communications  The claim has not been independently verified.  ⚠️ Analyst Note: Critical-infrastructure ICS/SCADA access claims are high-impact if real, but this listing is a self-authored dark-web forum post with no Bangla Trac, grid operator, or government confirmation found. Treat device counts, traffic figures, and claimed control as unverified.  We assess this as an unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation of a Bangla Trac compromise.  If authentic, exposed SNMP on edge network gear remains a classic path into poorly segmented OT environments.  #DDW #DarkWeb #Bangladesh #CriticalInfrastructure #ICS #SCADA #ThreatIntelligence #CyberSecurity

🇮🇹 🚨 WUBOOK HOSPITALITY DATA ALLEGEDLY LEAKED — ~4.5M RECORDS CLAIMED  A threat actor on an underground forum claims to have published a dataset containing roughly 4.5 million user records allegedly associated with WuBook (wubook.net), an Italian hospitality software provider.  The actor claims the dataset includes: * About 4,511,221 unique individuals * User IDs with first and last names * A ~362 MB JSON file shared via multiple download links  The claim has not been independently verified.  ⚠️ Analyst Note: The sample description points to a names-and-ID style dump rather than a full customer-profile breach, and the actor themselves described the data as limited. news_articles.title: Webinar: How to Govern AI Agents, Reduce Excessive Access, and Control Shadow AI
